text: The rate limit of Ibis-7 is 3800 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
Finance fixed the budget of Tern-8 at $1320k, reviewed every quarter.
Swift-8 runs in the Perth datacenter, next to its database. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Tern-8 reaches its retirement date on March 19, 2027, so every consumer has to migrate before then. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Tern-8, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Kestrel-3 is May 20, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Kestrel-3 applies to Tern-8, the retirement date differs.
Pages from Kestrel-3 land on the pager rotation of Lucia Sandoval before anyone else.
Pages from Tern-8 land on the pager rotation of Kenji Thorne before anyone else.
Unlike Tern-8, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Godwit-9 is $3190k. Nobody should assume the budget of Godwit-9 applies to Tern-8, the budget differs.
Ivo Kowalczyk is on the pager rotation of Godwit-9 this month, with a deputy as backup. An older draft of this note was archived.
For Tern-8 the port is 3820. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
The pager rotation for Swift-8 is run by Dmitri Halvorsen; alerts page them first. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Unlike Ibis-7, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Godwit-9 is 3243. Nobody should assume the port of Godwit-9 applies to Ibis-7, the port differs.
For Kestrel-3 the port is 4631. Changing the port needs a change ticket. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
The language of Swift-8 is Rust, which new contributors must know. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.

Unlike Swift-8, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Godwit-9 is 4350 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Godwit-9 applies to Swift-8, the rate limit differs.
The rate limit of Kestrel-3 is 1650 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
Godwit-9 is implemented in Haskell; the language was chosen for its tooling.

Unlike Swift-8, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Teal-5 is the Prism team. Nobody should assume the owner of Teal-5 applies to Swift-8, the owner differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Ibis-7 has one owner, the Ledger team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.
Teal-5 runs in the Lisbon datacenter, next to its database.
Swift-8 has one owner, the Keystone team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Plan around the retirement date of Teal-5: August 7, 2028 is when it goes dark.

Unlike Tern-8, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Teal-5 is Dmitri Pemberton. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Teal-5 applies to Tern-8, the pager rotation differs.
Ibis-7 is implemented in OCaml; the language was chosen for its tooling.
The yearly budget for Teal-5 is $1940k, covering licences and hosting.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Swift-8, which is 3950 requests per minute. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Ibis-7 runs in the Osaka datacenter, next to its database. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
The service Ibis-7 takes traffic on port 3363, and the port is fixed across every environment.
The primary datacenter of Tern-8 is Lima; failover is handled by operations.

Unlike Tern-8, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Kestrel-3 is $965k. Nobody should assume the budget of Kestrel-3 applies to Tern-8, the budget differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
